name: External work source (ticket or issue queue)
summary: A connection that lets the agent read, and optionally write, work items from an external tracker.
needed_when: Work lives in a ticket tracker and a person keeps copying it into the chat by hand.
detail: Register the tracker as an MCP server, give it read access first, and deny destructive calls such as delete in the permission rules.

name: Raw request triage (labels)
summary: A step that turns an unclear request into a labeled work type with a defined route.
needed_when: Requests arrive messy, or the same kind of work takes several different paths.
detail: Write a skill that reads the request, applies a small fixed label set, and states the next step for each label.

name: Clarify a request into a spec and tickets
summary: A question-and-answer sequence that ends in a spec and split tickets before work is handed off.
needed_when: The request is vague, has several stakeholders, or the user's choices never reach the profile, code or tests.
detail: Use an interview-style skill that asks one question at a time, then writes the spec and one ticket per vertical slice.

name: Work brief
summary: A written hand-off to a sub-agent: goal, scope, permissions, sources and done criteria.
needed_when: You delegate to an agent that cannot see your conversation.
detail: Keep a brief template with those five fields and fill it per task; do not fork the whole history.

name: Declared completion condition
summary: One "done when" sentence that a second party can check, optionally graded by another model after each turn.
needed_when: A multi-step task has an end state that can be verified, such as green tests or an empty queue.
detail: Put the condition in the brief; where the platform has a goal command, set it there so a separate check runs each turn.

name: Pushed events (webhook, push, trigger)
summary: Work that arrives on an event, such as a failed build, an opened pull request or a message, instead of waiting for a person to type.
needed_when: You want a reaction while you are away rather than periodic polling.
detail: Wire the event source to the platform trigger or scheduled task; keep the handler small and idempotent.

name: Remote and mobile entry
summary: Handing off or watching work from a phone, browser or chat without sitting at the machine.
needed_when: Long jobs run in the background on a desk machine and you are away.
detail: Enable the platform's remote-control or cloud-session feature; no custom code is needed.

name: Always-loaded project instructions
summary: A markdown file loaded every session with commands, conventions, architecture and "always do" rules.
needed_when: The agent gets the same convention wrong twice.
detail: Keep it short and as a pointer list; add a line each time a mistake repeats and link long guidance from the step that needs it.

name: Scope-based instructions
summary: Instructions that load only when the agent touches matching files or directories.
needed_when: A monorepo, or per-language or per-directory conventions.
detail: Use path-scoped rule files or nested instruction files so the root file stays small.

name: Precedence of overlapping instructions
summary: A stated rule for which layer wins when two instructions conflict.
needed_when: User, project, directory and organization instructions exist at the same time.
detail: Write down the order once; remember that most platforms merge layers and let the model reconcile conflicts, so avoid contradictory lines.

name: User-level and organization-level instructions
summary: Personal and organization-wide instruction layers that live outside the repository.
needed_when: Several projects share personal habits, or an organization wants common rules.
detail: Put personal habits in the user-level file and mandatory rules in the managed layer, never in each repo.

name: Auto-written memory
summary: Notes the agent writes itself from your corrections and preferences and reloads next session.
needed_when: You want fewer repeated reminders without hand-editing instructions.
detail: Enable the platform memory feature and review its notes now and then; promote stable ones into the instruction file.

name: Router and on-demand loading
summary: A short root instruction file that only points to the documents to read for each kind of task.
needed_when: The root instruction file exceeds the recommended size.
detail: Keep the root file under about 200 lines and link each topic file at the step that needs it.

name: Glossary and domain model
summary: One place that defines the terms and product concepts so the agent uses them with the right meaning.
needed_when: A specialist domain has words that mean different things in different places.
detail: Write a short glossary file, one line per term, and link it from the root instructions.

name: Reference store and source map
summary: Copies of, or pointers to, original material (designs, code, older snapshots) looked up when needed rather than preloaded.
needed_when: The true source sits in several repositories and the agent must know which one is authoritative.
detail: Keep a map file of pointers; grant read access to the extra directories only when a task needs them. For task-specific source selection, permitted access, representative use and continuation, read skills/harness/harness-evolve/CONTEXT.md relative to the plugin root; a catalog result alone does not establish usable context.

name: Reference skill
summary: A skill that holds lookup knowledge such as a guide or API notes rather than an action procedure.
needed_when: The knowledge is needed only sometimes and does not belong in the root file.
detail: Put the reference in a skill so only its short description loads each session and the body loads on use.

name: Context budget and compaction
summary: Limits on instruction size, conversation compaction, and control over what survives compaction.
needed_when: Long sessions, large instructions or large tool output.
detail: Keep critical instructions at the top of files, compact manually at task boundaries, and check what the platform re-reads after compaction.

name: Tool output filtering and limits
summary: Forcing tool results to be short, read in parts, with the full log kept outside the conversation.
needed_when: A command prints thousands of lines such as tests, logs or MCP listings.
detail: Make scripts print summaries by default with a flag for detail, and write full logs to a file.

name: Stable prompt-cache discipline
summary: Keeping the start of the prompt (tools, system text, instructions) unchanged during a session so caching works.
needed_when: Cost or latency is high in long sessions, or you switch model, effort or output style mid-session.
detail: Change model, effort and output style only at session boundaries and avoid editing instruction files mid-run.

name: Symbol-level code understanding (language server)
summary: Connecting a language server for jump-to-definition, find-references and immediate type errors after edits.
needed_when: Typed languages, large codebases, or grep that is slow or noisy.
detail: Install the platform's code-intelligence plugin for the language and confirm it reports an error after a deliberate bad edit.

name: External lookup and multi-source research
summary: Searching and reading web pages and combining them with citations.
needed_when: The task needs outside documentation or cross-checking of several sources.
detail: Use the built-in fetch and search tools or a research skill that records each source and how fully it was read.

name: Skill
summary: A directory with a SKILL.md (description, instructions, optional scripts or references) that the agent loads when relevant or when called by name.
needed_when: You paste the same multi-step procedure into chat for the third time.
detail: Write a short description that states when to trigger it, keep the body under about 500 lines, and move rare branches to linked files.

name: Control over who may invoke a skill
summary: Flags that decide whether a person types the skill or the model may pick it.
needed_when: The skill has side effects such as deploy or delete, or its listing takes context space.
detail: Mark side-effecting skills as user-invoked only and restrict their allowed tools in the frontmatter.

name: Isolated skill or dynamic-context skill
summary: A skill that runs in its own sub-agent, or that injects shell-command output into the skill body before the model sees it.
needed_when: The skill reads many files (avoid flooding the conversation) or needs live data such as a pull request diff.
detail: Set the skill to run in a forked context, or add a pre-run command whose output replaces a placeholder.

name: Slash command and reusable prompt
summary: A typed command that runs a saved prompt.
needed_when: You keep typing the same opening prompt for a task.
detail: Save the prompt as a user-invoked skill; most platforms have merged custom commands into skills.

name: System prompt customization
summary: Appending to or replacing part of the agent's system prompt at start-up.
needed_when: A role needs fixed instructions that do not belong in the repository.
detail: Use the platform's append-system-prompt flag or file in the launch command for that role.

name: Output style
summary: A set of instructions that fixes role, tone and format for every reply in a session.
needed_when: You always want shorter answers, always want explanations, or the agent is not a software engineer.
detail: Add a style file in the user or project styles folder and select it; changing it mid-session costs cache.

name: Role profile
summary: A named configuration bundle for one role: prompt, model, mode, thinking level, tools and skills.
needed_when: Several roles (coordinate, build, review) need different permissions and models.
detail: Define each role as a markdown file with frontmatter; point every field at something that exists.

name: "When to use which role" notes
summary: A short description that tells the coordinator which role to pick for which job.
needed_when: There are three or more roles and the coordinator is an agent.
detail: Fill each role's description field with the situations that should delegate to it.

name: Model, effort and thinking per role
summary: Each role runs with its own model and thinking level.
needed_when: Roles differ in cost or difficulty, such as heavy review versus light gathering.
detail: Set model and effort in the role profile and check the precedence rules for sub-agent models.

name: Shared working convention (mode)
summary: One skill or text loaded once for every role that sets the common way of working.
needed_when: Many roles need the same rhythm, such as loading principles, recording choices and reporting.
detail: Write one short mode skill and have each role profile load it first.

name: Principle (reusable judgment rule)
summary: A short principle such as "fix the root cause" or "prove it works" that the agent selects and states before the main action.
needed_when: You want consistent judgment and fewer repeated reasoning mistakes.
detail: Keep each principle as a small skill with a one-line trigger and a short procedure.

name: Autonomy switch (decide versus ask)
summary: A toggle between "the agent decides for the person" and "the agent asks first", set per ticket.
needed_when: Some work is safe to run autonomously and some needs a person's approval.
detail: Platforms offer this at the tool-call level through permission modes; a per-choice switch needs a small state file that your scripts read.

name: Plan before editing
summary: A read-only mode that proposes changes and edits only after a person approves the plan.
needed_when: The change is large or risky and the direction needs agreement first.
detail: Start the session in plan mode and approve the written plan before edits begin.

name: Role methodology document
summary: A document describing how one role works: sequence, checks and repeated errors.
needed_when: The role has a process longer than a profile page.
detail: Write one markdown file per role and link it from the router.

name: Lifecycle hook (foundation)
summary: A place to run a command, HTTP call, MCP tool, prompt or sub-agent at an agent lifecycle event.
needed_when: Something must happen every time without relying on the model to remember.
detail: Wire a small script to the event in settings; test it by triggering the event and reading the output.

name: Pre-tool gate (PreToolUse)
summary: A hook that inspects a command or file about to run and rejects it (exit 2) or rewrites it.
needed_when: A "never" rule such as editing secrets, recursive deletes, or writing into forbidden directories.
detail: Write a script that reads the tool call and exits 2 with a reason; test with the blocked action.

name: Post-edit hook (format, lint, quick test)
summary: An automatic check after each file edit whose result returns to the agent's context.
needed_when: You want lint or type errors visible as code is produced.
detail: Run the linter from a post-edit hook and print only failures so the output stays short.

name: Stop hook (force a check before finishing)
summary: A hook that runs when the agent is about to stop and can send it back to work or grade the done condition.
needed_when: "Done" must be verifiable and a self-report is not enough.
detail: Make the hook run the check command and block stopping while it fails, with a cap on repeats. Sources disagree here and this is not settled: one working standard holds that no check may block hard unless a recorded decision allows it (the "warn first, strict later" ladder, warn-before-blocking), so it avoids a blocking stop hook and instead has the launcher run the check on the final message and put any warning on the reporting path. Decide per harness which applies; this kit does not pick a side.

name: Session-start context hook
summary: A hook that prints extra context or prepares the environment when a session starts.
needed_when: You want a fixed bootstrap (load rules, check versions, check state) not left to reminders.
detail: Print only the few lines the agent needs; keep slow work out of the start-up path.

name: Automatic permission-approval hook
summary: A hook that answers permission requests on a person's behalf using rules you write.
needed_when: Unattended runs still need conditional approval.
detail: Allow a small named set of commands and deny the rest; log each answer.

name: Logging and notification hook
summary: An observe-only hook that logs, pushes notifications or sends telemetry without changing behavior.
needed_when: You need an audit trail or a message when work finishes.
detail: Keep it silent on stdout so it adds no context cost; write to a file or an endpoint.

name: Quality gate for agent teams
summary: Hooks that block marking work done, or a teammate going idle, until the work passes.
needed_when: You use agent teams or task lists and agents mark tasks done too early.
detail: Exit 2 from the task-completed hook with feedback that says which check failed.

name: Allow, ask and deny permission rules
summary: Rule lists per tool and command pattern, with a defined winner when they overlap.
needed_when: You need safe allowances (tests, lint) while still blocking sensitive files.
detail: Write allow rules for read-only and test commands, deny rules for secrets, and remember that deny wins at any scope.

name: Permission modes
summary: A session-wide level of automatic approval.
needed_when: The right level differs by work: exploring, hand-editing, long runs, locked-down CI.
detail: Pick the mode per role; use the bypass mode only inside an isolated container or VM.

name: Model-based automatic approver
summary: A classifier model that approves or denies at the permission boundary instead of a person.
needed_when: You want fewer prompts but still a block on irreversible actions.
detail: Enable the platform's auto mode, review its block list, and do not treat it as a guarantee of safety.

name: OS-level sandbox
summary: An operating-system boundary around shell commands for files and network.
needed_when: You want commands to run without asking each time while limiting harm.
detail: Enable the sandbox in settings, list the allowed paths and hosts, and test that a blocked write really fails.

name: File-scope fence
summary: A setting that blocks reading or writing outside the project directory.
needed_when: A role may only touch one directory tree.
detail: Turn on the block-outside-working-directory settings and add the few extra directories that are needed.

name: Per-role tool fence
summary: Each role gets only the tools it needs; the rest are removed from its context.
needed_when: A review role should be read-only, or a build role must not touch the ticket tracker.
detail: Set the tools and disallowed-tools fields in the role profile, not a sentence in the prompt.

name: Ban on tiered sub-agent spawning
summary: A rule on who may open sub-agents, enforced by removing the tool rather than by instruction.
needed_when: You have supervisor, orchestrator and worker tiers and do not want workers to spawn more.
detail: Deny the spawn tool for worker roles and set depth and concurrency limits in the launcher.

name: Outward writes need an explicit user statement
summary: Actions outside the repository (push, document store, tracker, delete) are done only when the user said so in this session, with the user's words logged.
needed_when: A mistaken write to an outside system is hard to undo.
detail: Add the rule to the role profile and require the quoted sentence in the log entry; platforms only offer per-tool prompts, so add a gate script if you need enforcement.

name: Secrets and identity
summary: How the agent obtains keys and tokens without them entering context or the sandbox.
needed_when: An MCP server or CLI needs credentials and several people share configuration.
detail: Use OAuth login or a helper command that produces the header at connect time; never put keys in instruction files.

name: Trust gate (folders, hooks, plugins)
summary: Repository-supplied configuration code runs only after a person confirms trust.
needed_when: You clone an unknown repository or accept plugins or hooks from others.
detail: Keep the trust prompt on, and in headless mode use the flag that skips project configuration unless you trust the folder.

name: Organization policy (managed settings)
summary: A top-priority configuration layer pushed by the organization that users cannot override.
needed_when: Many people or machines need the same limits on model, MCP, plugins and permissions.
detail: Deploy the managed settings file through your device management and test that a user setting cannot override it.

name: "Warn first, strict later" check ladder
summary: Every new check only warns (exit 0); it becomes a hard block (exit 1) only under a strict flag with a recorded reason.
needed_when: A new check is not yet proven to have few false alarms and a hard block could stall the flow.
detail: Give each checker a strict flag; run it in warn mode for a while and promote it when false alarms are rare.

name: Shared versus private boundary check
summary: A scanner that confirms shareable documents and code do not leak project-specific terms.
needed_when: A common standard set is carried between projects.
detail: Keep a forbidden-strings file outside the shared folder and run the scanner in strict mode on every change.

name: Hard caps: turns, budget, time, agent count
summary: Stop limits so a runaway cannot burn without end.
needed_when: Unattended runs, multi-agent workflows and scheduled jobs.
detail: Set max turns and max budget on every launch; add per-run caps to scheduled jobs.

name: Agent-to-agent trust is not user consent
summary: A rule that another agent's words do not replace a person's: no permission changes and no approvals on their behalf.
needed_when: Several agents message each other and you must stop permission escalation through messages.
detail: State the rule in every role profile; platforms that treat relayed approval as untrusted input already enforce part of it.

name: Criteria list that only flips a pass flag
summary: A JSON file listing every feature or criterion with a `passes` flag; the agent may only change false to true and never edits the description.
needed_when: The work spans many sessions and the agent tends to declare done early or delete hard criteria.
detail: Seed all items as false in the first session and use a tiny script or a hook that rejects any other change.

name: Progress log across sessions
summary: A file recording what was done, what is in progress and the next step, read first by the next session.
needed_when: Every session starts with empty context.
detail: Append one dated line per finished step with its evidence; the next session reads the last lines first.

name: Two phases: initialize, then work incrementally
summary: The first session builds the environment, spec and criteria list; later sessions advance one item at a time.
needed_when: The project is too large for one context window.
detail: Write two prompts, an initializer and a worker, and have the worker stop after one verified item.

name: Read before work, verify before continuing
summary: At the start of each session the agent must read the spec, list, log and git history and run regression tests before new work.
needed_when: The previous session may have left a defect.
detail: Make "get your bearings" and "run the verification test" the first two steps of the worker prompt.

name: Work lifecycle state machine
summary: The states and transitions of a work item: received, in which phase, awaiting review, done, sent back.
needed_when: Many tickets run in parallel across phases and you need to know where each stands.
detail: Describe the states in one document; add code only if you need transitions enforced.

name: Task list with dependencies and claiming
summary: An internal queue: create tasks, declare dependencies, agents claim ready tasks.
needed_when: Several parallel workers handle independent pieces.
detail: Use the platform's task list where available; claims must be locked so two workers cannot take one task.

name: Current-state file
summary: A single "current truth" file for a task, edited in place rather than stacking summaries.
needed_when: Context changes, agents change, or the conversation is compacted.
detail: Keep one file per task, overwrite stale facts, and link it from the brief. Maintenance adaptation: reuse adequate native stores; for linked corrections, serialized integration and scoped retention, read kit/MAINTENANCE.md.

name: Decision log and decision state machine
summary: A log of each choice made on a person's behalf: question, tentative pick, reason, approver, status, with record, review, audit and ready commands.
needed_when: An agent must choose for a person who reviews later and a "why" trail is needed.
detail: Write a small CLI over an append-only file; mark hard-to-reverse items so they need approval first. Maintenance adaptation: reuse adequate native stores; for linked corrections, serialized integration and scoped retention, read kit/MAINTENANCE.md.

name: Human approval gate (stop point)
summary: A mandatory point where a person looks and approves before work continues.
needed_when: A step is hard to reverse, or a phase changes.
detail: Name the gates in the workflow document and make the agent stop and ask there.

name: Structured output and result template
summary: Output in a fixed schema or template so a machine or parent agent can read it.
needed_when: A result feeds an automatic step or a hand-off between agents.
detail: Use the headless JSON output flags with a schema, and validate the result before use.

name: Recovery point (checkpoint and rewind)
summary: A snapshot of file state before each turn that allows undo.
needed_when: The agent damages several files.
detail: Rely on the platform's checkpoint feature, and commit before risky steps for what it does not cover.

name: Sessions: name, resume, fork
summary: Saved sessions that can be continued or branched to try another direction.
needed_when: Work spans days, or you want to try another approach from the same point.
detail: Name sessions, resume by name, and fork when exploring; resumed goals are restored.

name: Hand-off
summary: Moving the task and the context it needs to another agent or session.
needed_when: You change agent, change platform, or run out of context.
detail: Use a hand-off skill that writes goal, state, choices made and next step into one document.

name: Background agents and dashboard
summary: Sessions that run without a terminal, with one screen showing the status of many.
needed_when: Many independent jobs and you only want to step in when needed.
detail: Start work in the background mode and use the platform's agent view to see what needs input.

name: Run trace (transcript and logs)
summary: A full record of the conversation, commands and results for later lookup.
needed_when: Investigating an error or checking what was really done.
detail: Know where the platform stores session files and logs; use the debug flag when needed.

name: Retention and cleanup
summary: Rules for how long to keep things and what is cleaned automatically.
needed_when: Disk grows from scratch notes, snapshots and old worktrees.
detail: Set the platform retention period and add a cleanup script for old worktrees and notes. Maintenance adaptation: reuse adequate native stores; for linked corrections, serialized integration and scoped retention, read kit/MAINTENANCE.md.

name: Registry of running agents
summary: A record of which agents are running, whose, who the parent is, and the configuration fingerprint at spawn.
needed_when: Many agents run and you must know who the parent is to return results and which are stale.
detail: Use the platform's agent list if enough; otherwise write a small registry file updated at spawn and exit.

name: External systems through MCP
summary: A standard protocol for the agent to call tools and read data from outside systems (tickets, document store, database, browser).
needed_when: You keep copying data from a browser tab the agent cannot see.
detail: Register the server at the narrowest scope (local, project or user), prefer http transport, and let tool search load schemas on demand.

name: CLI or script the agent calls
summary: A command-line program in the repository that the agent runs through its shell tool.
needed_when: The outside system already has a CLI, or you need a repeatable, checkable action with short output.
detail: Prefer a CLI when one exists and keep MCP for systems without one; make output short and errors name the next step.

name: Skill with scripts
summary: A skill that bundles scripts or references its SKILL.md calls.
needed_when: An operation needs reliable code instead of the model rewriting it each time.
detail: Put the script in the skill folder, call it by the skill directory variable, and allow only the shell tool it needs.

name: Plugin (distribution package)
summary: A package of skills, agents, hooks, MCP servers and commands installed as one unit.
needed_when: A second repository needs the same setup.
detail: Add a manifest, group the components, and install with the platform's plugin command.

name: Marketplace and package versions
summary: A repository listing plugins to install, with versions or refs.
needed_when: You want to publish, update or restrict plugin sources.
detail: Publish a marketplace file that lists plugins and where to fetch each; pin versions for those you depend on.

name: Mods and interface extensions
summary: JavaScript hooks that can draw panes and add commands, or platform plugins that add screens, panels, slash commands and composer chips.
needed_when: You want to change the interface or behavior at the product layer, beyond configuration.
detail: Write the hooks module as a small plugin, test it in a throwaway profile, and keep it optional.

name: Programming SDK
summary: Using the agent as a library from your own program.
needed_when: You turn webhooks or issues into tasks, run many agents in parallel, or build a dashboard.
detail: Use the Python or TypeScript SDK, set max turns and budget, and log every run.

name: Headless run (exec)
summary: A one-shot run from a script or CI with structured output and correct exit codes.
needed_when: You embed the agent in a pipeline, a schedule or a hook.
detail: Run in print mode with JSON output and a schema, restrict allowed tools, and check the exit code.

name: Browser and computer control
summary: The agent opens pages, clicks, types and takes screenshots to check an interface.
needed_when: UI or web flows that unit tests cannot see.
detail: Connect a browser-automation MCP server or the platform's browser feature and have the agent capture evidence after each check.

name: Background progress monitor
summary: Run a command in the background and feed each output line back to the agent instead of polling.
needed_when: You wait on a build, a log or a push status and do not want to spend turns.
detail: Use the platform monitor tool with a command that prints one line per event.

name: Supervised long-running scripts and services
summary: Named scripts in configuration; long services are supervised with a port and a proxy.
needed_when: The agent must start a dev server, a database or long tests in the same workspace.
detail: Declare scripts in the workspace config, mark servers as services, and let the platform assign ports.

name: Role launcher
summary: A wrapper that builds the right flags, prompt, MCP, skills and permissions for each role at spawn; the single source of flags.
needed_when: Many roles need identical configuration on every spawn and you do not want to rely on people remembering flags.
detail: Keep the launcher thin: it reads the role profile and assembles the platform command line; test that it emits the expected flags.

name: Pin external tool versions
summary: Fixing the version of MCP servers, libraries and third-party skills.
needed_when: You want to avoid silent behavior change when an outside party ships a new release.
detail: Record exact versions in the config or lock file and re-check them when you upgrade.

name: Tool search on demand
summary: Load only tool names first and schemas when needed.
needed_when: Many MCP servers or tools bloat the context.
detail: Leave tool search on and remove unused servers.

name: Tool errors always name the next step
summary: Every error or limit message from a tool has a "fix:" line saying what to do next.
needed_when: The agent hits an error and either stops silently or guesses.
detail: Add a fix line to each error path in your scripts and test that it appears.

name: Sub-agent (isolated worker, returns a summary)
summary: A child agent with its own context, prompt, tools and permissions; only a summary returns.
needed_when: A side task floods the conversation with output you will not reference again.
detail: Define the sub-agent as a markdown file with a focused description and a narrow tool list.

name: Parallel sessions
summary: Several independent sessions at once, coordinated by hand or by an agent.
needed_when: There are several independent tasks that should not run in sequence.
detail: Give each session its own worktree and brief; collect results from files rather than from chat.

name: Agent team with task list and mailbox
summary: A lead and independent teammates that share a task list and message each other.
needed_when: The work needs teammates who discuss and challenge each other, not sequential steps.
detail: Enable the experimental feature, start with three to five teammates, and give each a different file set.

name: Dynamic workflow (orchestration script)
summary: A script the agent writes that drives tens to hundreds of sub-agents and returns one result.
needed_when: The work exceeds a few sub-agents or needs cross-checked results, such as a repository-wide audit.
detail: Let the platform's workflow feature generate the script, review it before running, and cap concurrency.

name: Messaging between sessions and agents
summary: A channel for one agent to send text to another agent or session (not history).
needed_when: One session breaks something another depends on, or one session settles a question another is blocked on.
detail: Use the platform's cross-session messaging; keep messages short and self-contained.

name: Parent-child relay
summary: A process that follows child agents and pushes their final report to the parent, with logging and a "delivered" state.
needed_when: The parent does not want to poll and the child must report automatically when done.
detail: Write a small watcher or use the sub-agent-stop event to deliver the last message and mark it delivered.

name: Coordination tiers and width limits
summary: A tree of roles (supervisor, orchestrator, worker): who may open whom and how many.
needed_when: Many tickets and phases need one point of contact with the user.
detail: Document the tiers and enforce the limits in the launcher rather than in prose.

name: Maintenance inbox for the harness keeper
summary: A fixed folder where any role leaves "work only the maintainer can do"; items move to a read folder once handled.
needed_when: An agent finds a harness defect but is not allowed to fix it itself.
detail: Define the folder and a one-file-per-item format; the maintainer clears it on a schedule.

name: Multi-provider coordination
summary: Choosing different agent providers for different jobs in one frame.
needed_when: You want cross-opinions or each provider's strengths.
detail: Use a platform or MCP server that can launch several providers and keep the role profile independent of the provider.

name: Advisor, second opinion, committee
summary: Asking a stronger model, or two independent agents, at a hard point.
needed_when: You are about to commit to a direction, are stuck on a repeating failure, or about to declare done.
detail: Use an advisor skill that sends a compact brief and returns a recommendation; do not let it do the work.

name: Queue for messages to a busy session
summary: Messages sent while the agent works wait and run after the current turn.
needed_when: A coordinator sends more work before the child finishes.
detail: Use the platform's queued send and do not assume the message was read mid-turn.

name: Multi-machine coordination
summary: Running agents on another machine, linked by SSH, relay or a private network, managed by a hub.
needed_when: A powerful remote machine, or a shared team setup.
detail: Use the platform's remote or hub feature and treat each machine as a separate trust boundary.

name: Runnable check (tests, typecheck, CI)
summary: Giving the agent a way to verify its own answer.
needed_when: Always; the done criterion must be something that runs.
detail: State the check command in the brief and require its output as evidence; fix the code, not the test.

name: Eval for harness artifacts
summary: A set of graded test cases for skills, plugins, prompts and roles, rerun when the harness or the model changes.
needed_when: You change a skill, instruction or role profile and cannot tell if quality dropped.
detail: Write cases as prompt plus grader (pattern, tool called, or rubric) and run them with the platform's eval command where one exists.

name: Automatic and local code review
summary: An agent reads a diff or pull request and verifies findings before reporting.
needed_when: Before merge, to catch logic, security and edge-case defects.
detail: Use the review skill or the platform's review action and have it verify each finding.

name: Independent reviewer; builder does not self-grade
summary: Changes to behavior-controlling files must be graded by another agent or person.
needed_when: You edit instruction files, profiles, skills or the launcher.
detail: Add a reviewer role with read-only tools; note that sources disagree on whether sub-agent verification helps, so measure it.

name: Security scan while writing code
summary: The agent reviews its own change for vulnerabilities and fixes them in the same session.
needed_when: You want less security-review load later.
detail: Install the platform's security-guidance plugin or add a short checklist step to the worker prompt.

name: Stale-agent detection by configuration fingerprint
summary: At spawn, store a hash of prompt, settings, MCP, skills and launcher flags; later compare with the current hash to learn that a running agent uses outdated configuration.
needed_when: You edit a profile or skill mid-run and old agents keep running the old version.
detail: Hash the inputs at spawn into the registry and report a mismatch in the status view.

name: Effective configuration and dry run
summary: A command that prints the configuration that would really be used (which source wins, which flags) without running.
needed_when: You suspect configuration did not apply, or want to check before spawning.
detail: Use the platform status and doctor commands, or write a print-only mode in the launcher.

name: Quality audit of instructions and skills
summary: A tool that inspects instructions and skills for length, contradiction and vague descriptions.
needed_when: Instructions grow, or skill descriptions overlap.
detail: Run the platform audit command, or a small script that measures description length and flags duplicates.

name: Cost and usage measurement
summary: Tokens and money per session, role and day.
needed_when: You run many agents and need caps and alerts.
detail: Read the cost fields from JSON output, aggregate per role, and add a cap to the launcher.

name: Telemetry (OpenTelemetry)
summary: Export metrics, events and traces to an observability backend.
needed_when: Production or team use where you must know what agents do.
detail: Turn on the platform's telemetry export and point it at a collector.

name: Tests for the harness itself
summary: Automated tests for the launcher, checkers and tools of the harness.
needed_when: The harness has code you wrote.
detail: Write small tests that run each checker on good and bad samples and assert the exit code and message.

name: Turn an incident into a test case
summary: Each incident produces an eval or test so it is caught next time.
needed_when: A defect repeats or slipped through review.
detail: Add a line to the incident log and a matching case in the check set before closing the incident.

name: Regression on model or system-prompt change
summary: Rerun checks when a new model ships or the harness changes, and remove obsolete components.
needed_when: You upgrade the model or notice quality shift.
detail: Keep a fixed check set and rerun it on every model or prompt change; record the scores.

name: Re-read the live source before writing (unattended jobs)
summary: Before recording state, read the source again; a failed source is reported as "unreadable", not "nothing new".
needed_when: Scheduled jobs that pull outside data.
detail: Make the job distinguish a read error from an empty result and write the error to the log.

name: Evidence rule (stated, inferred, open)
summary: A reporting rule that separates what the source says, what is inferred and what is unchecked; check the real artifact at the right revision.
needed_when: An agent reports to another agent or to a person who decides.
detail: Require every claim to carry one of the three labels and a source or command output.

name: Commit and pull-request gate
summary: A command that checks commit trailers and stray lines before merge.
needed_when: The target project has commit or pull-request conventions.
detail: Run the checker in warn mode first and promote to strict once false alarms are rare.

name: Verify by driving the real app
summary: A skill that sets up how to run the app like a user and proves behavior.
needed_when: The project has no scripted way to verify UI, CLI or service behavior.
detail: Write the launch steps and a checklist in the skill and combine it with browser control.

name: Retrospective (after-action review)
summary: A look back at a session or task that draws lessons and proposes changes to skills, instructions or profiles.
needed_when: The same kind of error repeats, or at the end of a batch of work.
detail: Use a retro skill that proposes edits for a person to accept; do not let it rewrite instructions silently.

name: "Wrong twice, write it down" rule
summary: When an agent errs the same way twice or review repeats a comment, edit the instruction or skill instead of correcting in chat.
needed_when: Always; this is the trigger for learning.
detail: Add the rule to the root instructions and act on it at the second occurrence.

name: Encode a lesson in structure, not more text
summary: A priority order for preventing repeat errors: architecture, types, a lint whose message names the fix, a test, and documentation last.
needed_when: You wrote the same reminder a second time.
detail: Try the earliest option in the order that can enforce the rule; write the doc line only if none can.

name: Failure-class catalog
summary: A table classifying the errors seen (design, build, operation, verification) to show distribution and gaps.
needed_when: You want to know where the harness breaks most.
detail: Keep one table with a row per class and a count; update it from each incident. A workable starting set: A. Wrong text (contradictions, stale wording left after a rule change); B. Inefficient tools (wasted context, duplicate messages, state files never cleaned up); C. Stale running agents (prompt, config or tool changed but a live agent did not reload); D. Not reviewable later (no history, drifting commit codes); E. Outside A-D (state or gate models that drift from the user's intent, role and channel fences, skipped procedures, harness versus product boundary). Give each class one general prevention and attach real examples in the project's own document.

name: Prune components when a new model ships
summary: Periodically remove each harness component and re-measure whether it is still needed.
needed_when: You upgrade the model, or the harness has grown heavy.
detail: Remove one component at a time, rerun the check set, and keep the removal if scores hold.

name: Measured improvement (hill-climbing)
summary: Editing prompts or skills in a loop with scores, separate train and test sets, and a noise measurement first.
needed_when: You have an eval set and want a controlled score increase.
detail: Measure run-to-run noise before changing anything and accept a change only when it beats the noise on held-out cases. For bounded cost/latency diagnosis or learning with explicit quality and adoption limits, read skills/harness/harness-evolve/EXPERIMENT.md relative to the plugin root.

name: Maintenance loop by the harness keeper
summary: A procedure for editing the harness: log before coding, reread with a command, measure before fixing, fix the tool instead of adding a second check.
needed_when: The harness has a dedicated keeper.
detail: Write the loop as a short checklist in the maintainer's document.

name: In-session loop (recurring prompt)
summary: Re-run a prompt on a cycle inside an open session.
needed_when: Watching a pull request, build or deploy while you work.
detail: Use the platform loop command with an interval; prefer a monitor when events can push.

name: Durable schedule
summary: A schedule that runs with no session open: cloud, desktop or daemon.
needed_when: A weekly retro, a morning triage or branch cleanup.
detail: Create a cloud scheduled task with a prompt, repositories and connectors; set a cost cap.

name: Heartbeat (wake an existing agent)
summary: A recurring prompt sent into one existing agent so it reassesses and continues the same conversation.
needed_when: Watching a long build or CI in the same conversation.
detail: Create the heartbeat through the platform tool and set a modest interval.

name: CI/CD integration
summary: Running the agent inside a pipeline on a pull request, an issue or a schedule.
needed_when: You want automatic pull-request review or pull requests generated from issues.
detail: Use the platform's CI action, limit its permissions and secrets, and require a status check.

name: Unattended run: permissions and caps
summary: Configuration so a scheduled job does not hang on a permission dialog or burn without limit.
needed_when: Any background job, including loops, schedules, heartbeats, and CI/CD runs.
detail: Set the no-prompts permission mode with an explicit allow list and set turn and cost caps.

name: Bookmark and source state for scheduled jobs
summary: The job remembers how far it read from each source rather than "the last 24 hours".
needed_when: Pulling issues or documents on a schedule.
detail: Store a per-source marker; on a read error keep the old marker and report "unreadable".

name: Notifications
summary: Telling a person when attention is needed or work is done.
needed_when: Long background work while the person is away.
detail: Use the platform's push-notification tool or a notification hook.

name: Live monitoring and agent lifetime
summary: Alerts when an agent runs too long or hangs.
needed_when: Many background agents.
detail: Set a time limit and a restart policy for silent agents; alert after the limit.

name: Recovery after a crash or restart
summary: What happens to background work when a process dies or the machine shuts down.
needed_when: Long-running jobs.
detail: Write state to a file after each step so a restarted job resumes; note that most schedulers do not catch up on missed runs.

name: Remote and cloud execution
summary: A session that runs on another machine or in the cloud and continues when you close your laptop.
needed_when: Long work and a desk machine that cannot stay open.
detail: Start a cloud session from the platform; keep secrets in its environment settings.

name: Staged release of harness changes
summary: Putting a harness change into use through a channel with rollback.
needed_when: The harness has many users or projects.
detail: There is no official canary channel; version the harness, roll out to one project first and keep the previous version for rollback.

name: Upgrade procedure (model, CLI, pinned skills)
summary: A check procedure when the model or CLI version changes.
needed_when: The CLI is upgraded, for example a version that ignores a settings file.
detail: After each upgrade run the effective-configuration command and the check set.

name: Layered configuration scopes
summary: The same key can be set at user, project, local and managed levels with a clear winner.
needed_when: Individuals want overrides that stay out of the repository, or an organization wants enforcement.
detail: Learn the scope order once and place each setting at the lowest level that fits.

name: Share through git
summary: Commit configuration, skills, hooks and agents so the whole team gets the same version.
needed_when: The team has more than one person.
detail: Commit the project settings and skills; keep personal overrides in the local file that is git-ignored.

name: Common standard and project-specific part
summary: Separating a standard that can move to other projects from the project's own part.
needed_when: Several projects share a harness.
detail: Keep the shared part in its own folder with a boundary check, and let each project add a thin private layer.

name: Multi-machine, multi-person hub
summary: A layer above daemons: machine registry, triggers, event record, sharing.
needed_when: A team shares several machines.
detail: Use the platform's hub feature and keep triggers in the repository.

name: Audit log
summary: A trace sufficient to answer "which agent did what, under which choice".
needed_when: Compliance, incidents, or disputes over a choice.
detail: Log each tool call with its allow, ask or deny result, an identity and a request id, kept apart from content.

name: Share outputs and onboarding guides
summary: Export results as a viewable page, send files, create a guide for teammates.
needed_when: The result is clearer visually than as text, or a new teammate joins.
detail: Use the platform's artifact and file-send features; no code is needed.

name: File ownership per agent
summary: Each agent owns its own set of files so no two edit the same file.
needed_when: Several parallel workers share one repository.
detail: Assign file sets in the brief and break work along those lines.

name: Roles and membership permissions
summary: Who in the organization may use which feature.
needed_when: Many people and permissions must be separated, such as cloud sessions.
detail: Use the platform's role and workspace permission settings.

name: Git worktree per task
summary: A separate directory and branch for each session or agent so they do not trample each other.
needed_when: Several tasks in parallel on one repository.
detail: Create one worktree per task with the platform flag or a git command, and remove it when merged.

name: Workspace (project, workspace, session)
summary: An organizing unit around the place of work instead of around a chat.
needed_when: One task needs several sessions, terminals, a browser and diffs in one place.
detail: Use the platform's workspace feature; one workspace per task.

name: Environment lifecycle: setup, teardown, ignored files to copy
summary: Commands run when a worktree is created or removed, and a list of ignored files to copy over (such as an env file).
needed_when: A new worktree lacks dependencies and local configuration.
detail: Put setup and teardown commands in the workspace config and list the files to copy.

name: Per-task resources (database, port)
summary: Each ticket gets its own database or port, with locks on shared ones to prevent overlap.
needed_when: Tests use a real database and several agents run in parallel.
detail: Derive the database name and port from the ticket id and refuse to start if it is taken.

name: Source data mirror
summary: Pull outside data into a local copy used as a stable read source instead of reading live.
needed_when: The source is in a document store and runs must be repeatable.
detail: Write a sync script that pulls into a mirror folder and stamps the date of the copy.

name: Vendoring and dependency copies
summary: Keeping a copy of outside code or skills inside the repository so runs repeat.
needed_when: You do not want to depend on network or outside versions; it costs space and can drift.
detail: Vendor only what you must, record the upstream version, and check for drift on a schedule.

name: Machine isolation (container, VM)
summary: Running the agent in a disposable environment so broad permissions are acceptable.
needed_when: You use bypass mode or an untrusted agent.
detail: Use a dev container or VM without internet access for bypass-mode runs.

name: Rule against overwrites when merging worktrees
summary: A concrete rule about symlinks to ignored folders that overwrite real folders when merged.
needed_when: A worktree needs data from ignored folders such as vendor or data.
detail: Write the rule in the worktree guide: never merge a symlink to an ignored folder; git tracks the link and on merge it overwrites the real folder. Point at the data by absolute path in the command or by an environment variable instead. Completion condition: before merging, `git diff --stat <target-branch>...HEAD` lists only the files meant to change, and `git diff --summary` shows no file mode 120000 (symlink).

name: Status line
summary: A bar at the bottom of the interface that runs your script and receives session JSON on stdin.
needed_when: You want context use, cost, git branch or session name always visible.
detail: Write a short script that reads the JSON and prints one line.

name: Multi-session overview and progress
summary: One place to see the state of many agents: running, needs you, done.
needed_when: Many background sessions.
detail: Use the platform's agent view; it is a human interface, separate from a registry.

name: Result template and brief template
summary: Fixed forms for hand-off reports and for delegated tasks.
needed_when: Many agents return results to a parent and the parent needs to read and compare quickly.
detail: Keep two small template files and reference them from the role profiles.

name: Report with sources and certainty labels
summary: A research report format: source (id, URL, date read), verbatim quote, and a split of "stated / inferred / open".
needed_when: A report is the basis for a choice.
detail: Define the table columns once and require them in every research hand-off.

name: Presentation conventions (language, paths)
summary: Fixed rules for language, absolute paths and backtick use.
needed_when: Many agents write for the same reader.
detail: Write the rules in the root instructions or an output style.

name: Design documents, ADRs and specs
summary: Written records of architectural choices and specifications.
needed_when: A choice is hard to reverse and the reason must be kept.
detail: Use one short file per choice with question, options, reason and consequence.

name: Commit and pull-request text
summary: A fixed form for commit messages (trailers) and pull-request bodies.
needed_when: The target project's conventions require it.
detail: Use a PR-writing skill and a commit template; add a checker if the convention is strict.

name: Conventions for writing agent documents (one idea one place, length)
summary: General rules for writing for agents: short, each idea once, pointers instead of copies, neutral examples.
needed_when: Documents grow and contradict each other.
detail: Keep files short, link instead of copy, and give each rule one home.

name: Harness review checklist
summary: A fixed six-point list that an independent reviewer applies to every change touching files that steer agent behavior.
needed_when: A change touches agent-steering files (root instructions, role profiles, skill bodies, launcher, checkers) and the author must not grade it alone.
detail: Run it in a separate reviewer role with a clean context that receives the diff since the previous review plus the choices approved in that range; score all six points even when one has no finding. 1) When a concept is renamed, changed or dropped, search the whole repo for the old wording and contradicting sentences. 2) One source of truth: pointers, not a second copy of a rule. 3) Every step has a completion condition of the right kind (a checkable one for fragile or side-effecting steps, goal and constraints for judgment steps); text says what to do; each prohibition carries its reason and the replacement action. 4) Text matches code: commands, flags, paths and `fix:` messages exist and are still right (run with `--help` or try them, do not only read). 5) Tests check behavior (exit code, output, files produced), not document wording. 6) Approved choices show in both text and code; name which components need a fresh agent and which live agents will now be stale. The report does not block; one pass per work item. Where the reviewer role lives, where its report is written and how it is opened are project-specific.

name: Team responsibilities and review
summary: Usable roles, reviewer context, authority and independence for manual or agent collaboration.
needed_when: Responsibility or reviewer identity is unclear; team-only work needs a result without workflow setup.
detail: Read kit/team-workflow/TEAM.md relative to the plugin root. Reuse existing actors and grants; distinguish reviewer identity/context/authority/independence from workflow timing and handoffs. Missing source access or independence blocks the dependent review, not all work.

name: Task contracts and selected flow
summary: Accessible task definitions, transitions, policy, trackers and conditional flow controls.
needed_when: Manual or single-agent workflow needs usable tasks, review handoffs, flow choices or tracker guidance.
detail: Read kit/team-workflow/TASKS.md relative to the plugin root; follow FLOW.md for selected flow and TRACKERS.md for source/tracker choices. Resolve effective values within actual grants. Manual work is valid; declared controls are not enforcement evidence.

name: Instruction and response design
summary: Reconciled guidance, usable examples and externally testable model-output criteria.
needed_when: A direct instruction, handoff or response-contract request needs a result; guidance sources conflict.
detail: Read kit/instruction-response/DESIGN.md relative to the plugin root. Resolve actual authority before dependent use; apply current original writing and scoped STE-inspired guidance. Preserve consumer language and distinguish content/form acceptance from exchanged tool protocol validity.

name: Authority design and calibration
summary: PSW function ceilings, delegated-choice review, outcome-based calibration and concrete effect/grant choices.
needed_when: Direct authority design or calibration; proposed effects need grant resolution; legacy delegation needs reconciliation.
detail: Read kit/authority/DESIGN.md relative to the plugin root. Preserve the ten-level reference and qualified alternatives; keep task stage separate from function ceilings. Actual grants and native constraints bind effects. Use prior adoption authority and selected recording/review controls.

name: Standards selection and document checks
summary: Applicable requirements, conflicts and useful machine or human checks, with selected, performed and satisfied states.
needed_when: A direct standards request or document work needs usable criteria and honest accuracy review.
detail: Read kit/standards/SELECT.md and its document branch through setup/evolve. Reuse selected material, preserve consumer language and prior replacement authority, and separate check execution from satisfaction. All six document families are available; human-only source facts retain required human accuracy review. Team and workflow own reviewers and handoffs; assessment interprets evidence. No factory setup or blanket stage ceiling follows.

name: Optional factory arrangement
summary: Connect selected services, tasks, authority, controls and recovery with evidence-scoped readiness.
needed_when: The consumer explicitly selects factory design, application or unattended-readiness assessment.
detail: Read kit/FACTORY.md through setup/evolve. Reuse task/flow, authority, operation, observation and recovery contracts. Preserve selected original methods, stage, brakes, andon, review and approval. Separate design, authorized application and observed unattended use; manual fallback cannot qualify unattended operation.
